text:
maya: hi all, quick intro — Maya here, starting today. I can log into Console but the feature flags tab shows restricted. Who do I ask to get staging flag-manager access?

onboard-bot: Welcome @maya! See onboarding step: Platform access -> Console. If missing groups, open an access request.

chris_ops: hey Maya, welcome :wave: We add new hires to redwood-console-staging-managers during provisioning but sometimes it gets missed. I'll check. Can you confirm your work email?

maya: maya@redwood.com

chris_ops: thanks. Opening a manual ticket now. If you need to run ffctl locally, request a scoped service account tagged "ffcli-temp".

olivia: adding: staging role is quick (manager approval only). Prod requires security review + justification. Also make sure your SSO groups are reflected in Okta - logging out/in helps.

chris_ops: ticket ACC-5011 created. Approvers: manager @olivia. ETA ~15m for manual grant.

maya: thanks! also, for the SA — how are credentials shared? I don't want secrets posted in the channel.

chris_ops: we'll create the SA and put the key into the onboarding vault under path: secret/onboarding/sa/maya-ffcli. You get read access for 7 days. Rotate using `vault renew <path>` if you need more time.

olivia: one more caveat: ffctl tokens expire after 7 days. Use `ffctl auth refresh` to re-auth. For prod-level token requests, include a short justification in the access form.

onboard-bot: Docs updated: https://docs.redwood.com/onboarding/console-flags. Reminder: enable 2FA before requesting infra grants.

chris_ops: manual grant completed. You should see Flags -> Manage now. If you still see 403, try clearing site data or re-auth.

maya: confirmed, I can open the flags manager and list flags. I filed the SA request too. Thank you all! :smile:

olivia: welcome aboard! If you want a quick walkthrough on flag rollout flow, ping me and I'll DM a demo.

maya: will do, appreciate it :pray:
